_comment: MoE routing and load-balancing constants. Charter docs/standards/moe_0905.md;
THE TWO ENTRIES HERE ARE PAPER-REPORTED, NOT MEASURED BY US. They are DeepSeek-V3's
published hyper-parameters, read out of arXiv:2412.19437 on 2026-09-05, at a scale 60x
ours in tokens per expert per step. status is `recorded` for exactly that reason: nothing
in this repo has measured either constant, and each entry's boundary field states the gap
in its own words rather than relying on this note.

facts.value: DeepSeek-V3's aux-loss-free load balancer updates a per-expert bias by a fixed step size gamma = 0.001 for the first 14.3T tokens, then 0.0 for the remaining 500B (i.e. the bias is FROZEN for the last 3.4% of the 14.8T-token run). The bias is added to the affinity score for top-k SELECTION ONLY -- 'Note that the bias term is only used for routing', and 'The gating value, which will be multiplied with the FFN output, is still derived from the original affinity score'. Update rule: at the end of each step, 'decrease the bias term by gamma if its corresponding expert is overloaded' and 'increase it by gamma if its corresponding expert is underloaded'. Overload is judged over the whole training-step batch, not per sequence.
facts.source: arXiv:2412.19437 (DeepSeek-V3 technical report), section 2.1.2 for the rule and the routing-only scope (eq. 16), section 4.2 Training Hyper-Parameters for the value; read from https://arxiv.org/html/2412.19437 on 2026-09-05, quotes above verbatim from that text. Relayed by 4c and re-read independently before this entry was written.

config.their_scale: 671B total / 37B activated, 61 layers, 256 routed + 1 shared experts per MoE layer, 8 routed activated per token, expert intermediate dim 2048, model dim 7168, FFN replaced by MoE in all but the first three layers, 14.8T tokens, seq 4K, batch 3072 -> 15360 sequences over the first 469B tokens then constant
config.their_tokens_per_expert_per_step: 1,966,080 at the steady-state batch (15360 x 4096 x 8 / 256) and 393,216 at the warmup batch (3072 sequences) -- computed here from the reported batch schedule, NOT stated in the paper
config.gamma_is_not_a_gradient: the bias is updated from measured load, not by backprop, so gamma is a step size on a control loop and does not scale with the optimizer's lr

facts.uncertainty: None reported. The paper gives one value for one run and no sweep, no ablation over gamma, and no sensitivity curve, so nothing here bounds how wrong a different gamma would be.
facts.boundary: PAPER-REPORTED AT 60x OUR PER-EXPERT TOKEN COUNT. Our E1 arm sees 32,768 tokens per routed expert per step (262,144 tokens/step, top-3, 24 routed experts) against their 1,966,080 -- a factor of 60.0, and still 12.0x below even their warmup batch. gamma controls how fast the balancer corrects a load imbalance, and the imbalance signal it reads is a per-expert token count whose relative noise grows as that count shrinks, so their value carries no guarantee at our scale. It is also 24 routed experts against 256, 12 layers against 61, and 1B tokens against 14.8T. Adopting 0.001 is borrowing a starting point, not inheriting a result.

facts.value: DeepSeek-V3 also carries a complementary SEQUENCE-WISE balance loss with coefficient alpha = 0.0001, alongside the aux-loss-free bias: 'For the balance loss, we set alpha to 0.0001, just to avoid extreme imbalance within any single sequence.' It is L_Bal = alpha * sum_i f_i * P_i (eq. 17), with f_i the fraction of the sequence's tokens routed to expert i and P_i the mean normalised affinity over that sequence's T tokens. Its stated purpose is per-sequence extremes only, not global balance -- global balance is the bias's job.
facts.source: arXiv:2412.19437 section 2.1.2 (eq. 17 and the motivation, 'which will be assigned an extremely small value for DeepSeek-V3') and section 4.2 for alpha = 0.0001; read from https://arxiv.org/html/2412.19437 on 2026-09-05.

config.relationship_to_the_bias: COMPLEMENTARY, not an alternative: the aux-loss-free bias handles balance across the step's batch, this loss handles imbalance within one sequence. Reporting the design as purely aux-loss-free omits this term.
config.their_scale: same run as moe.dsv3_bias_update_speed -- 256 routed experts, 8 active, seq 4K

facts.uncertainty: None reported: one value, no sweep, no ablation isolating this term's contribution from the bias's.
facts.boundary: PAPER-REPORTED, and its scale argument differs from the bias's. This loss is per SEQUENCE, so what matters is tokens per sequence per expert: at seq 4096 with top-3 over 24 experts we get 512 tokens per expert per sequence against their 4096 x 8 / 256 = 128, i.e. our per-sequence signal is 4x THEIRS even though our per-step signal is 60x worse. So this term's regime is closer to comparable than the bias's, but it is still unmeasured here and it is not registered as part of the moe_0905 arms.

facts.value: On CUDA at bf16, torch._grouped_mm's reduction order differs from an identical plain matmul computing the SAME function by max|d| = 0.001953. fp32-on-CUDA and plain-matmul-at-bf16 both give exactly 0.0, so the difference belongs to the grouped kernel's reduction, not to bf16. On CPU the same comparison is exactly 0.0 at both fp32 and bf16.
facts.source: tilerl on card 7, via scripts/moe_dispatch_bench.py's tied-weights witness (the measurement that made the witness's own 1e-3 tolerance refuse a correct module); CPU side reproduced by b0 in scripts/test_moe_module.py's harness. FOUND BY tilerl, credited here because the number is theirs.

config.why_it_matters: any numerical-agreement assertion at or below 1e-3 REFUSES A CORRECT MODULE when run on the card. Two witnesses were calibrated on CPU where the floor is 0.0 and would have failed on CUDA: tilerl's bench witness (fixed to 4e-3) and b0's scripts/test_moe_module.py (checks 1 and 3, now 1e-2 on CUDA and 1e-6/1e-5 on CPU, ruled by 4c).
config.defect_signals_this_must_stay_below: 0.0172 for swapped SiTU-GLU betas and 0.023 for plain a*sigmoid(b) in place of SiTU-GLU, both on outputs of scale ~0.7 -- these are FUNCTION differences and do not shrink with precision, which is what makes a band between the floor and them possible at all
config.chosen_bounds: bench 4e-3 (2x the floor); module tests 1e-2 on CUDA (~5x the floor, still 1.7x below the smaller defect), 1e-6/1e-5 on CPU where the floor is 0.0

facts.uncertainty: ONE shape on ONE card, single measurement, no repeat and no spread. The floor may differ with expert count, group sizes, or a torch version -- which is why the chosen bound sits several multiples above it rather than at 2x.
facts.boundary: measured for _grouped_mm at bf16 on the pod's card at the bench's shape. It says nothing about _scaled_grouped_mm (fp8), nothing about other reduction sizes, and nothing about the backward pass -- the witness compares forward outputs only.

facts.value: At matched tokens the 8B-token MoE-48 arm is WORSE than the dense 0.2b arm at all five measured points, by +0.6680 nat at 0.16B narrowing to +0.0380 at 0.79B. The gap closes fast and monotonically over the first four pairs; the fifth is +0.0380 against +0.0370, so no direction is claimed past 0.63B.
facts.source: eval/equal_token_gap.py (--selftest pins both curves as known answers; no argument reads the logs). Logs live ON THE POD, not in the repo, read through ~/bin/pod. THE ARM'S LOG IS IN TWO SEGMENTS and reading only the first returns a table that is short without saying so: /work/aupai/runs/b0_moe48_8b.log ends at step 1000 with SignalException signal 15 (b0_moe48_8b.rc holds 1) and the run continues in /work/aupai/runs/1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.log, whose line 29 is a Resumed-from naming the first segment's step-1000 checkpoint, under an identical cfg line and the same total 10172. The verbatim resume line is quoted in eval/equal_token_gap.py's ARM_LOGS comment; NO CHECKPOINT IS A SOURCE OF THIS FACT -- the two logs are, and the resume is named only to say why one log is not the whole run. The instrument reads both in order (its ARM_LOGS) and refuses a segment whose cfg tok/step disagrees. Comparator log: /work/aupai/runs/b0_e1p_dense.log. Run rows in runs/experiments.jsonl under names b0_moe48_8b and b0_e1p_dense. Balancer diagnostics in runs/moe_diag.jsonl (name moe48_8b). Reproduced by the instrument against the live logs on 2026-09-06: 5 of 5 pairs exact, and re-run after the two-segment fix the same day it reads 9 val points to arm step 1800 and reproduces all 5 -- the value above is unchanged by the fix.

config.arm: b0_moe48_8b -- 48 routed experts, top_k 3, expert_ffn 768, 1 shared, moe_layers 0-11, moe_bias_gamma 0.001, dim 1024 L12 h8 ffn3072, max_steps 10172
config.comparator: b0_e1p_dense -- no moe_* keys in its cfg line, i.e. the dense 0.2b recipe at batch 64
config.pairing_rule: b0_moe48_8b runs at global batch 192 (batch 8 x accum 4 x 6 cards) = 786,432 tokens/step; both comparators run at global batch 64 (16 x accum 2 x 2 cards) = 262,144 tokens/step. Ratio exactly 3, so MoE step N is compared with the comparator's step 3N and the comparison is at MATCHED TOKENS, not matched steps. The ratio is read off each log's own cfg line rather than assumed, and the pairing is confirmed by the logs' token counters: the comparators print 0.16B / 0.31B / 0.47B / 0.63B / 0.79B at steps 600 / 1200 / 1800 / 2400 / 3000, which is what MoE steps 200 / 400 / 600 / 800 / 1000 print. MATCHED-STEP PAIRING REVERSES THE SIGN against the dense arm (-0.439 to -0.269, i.e. the MoE arm apparently ahead everywhere), which is why the instrument asserts the ratio instead of trusting it.
config.shared: All three arms: same mix data/mix_200m_8b.json, same seed 42, seq 4096, doc_mask True, attn_res True, softcap 15.0, warmdown 0.1, anneal_frac 0, val_every 200, bf16, no grad_ckpt. Read from each log's cfg line, not from the launch command.
config.sign: positive = the 8B-token MoE arm's val is HIGHER, i.e. worse, at that token count

facts.uncertainty: FIVE PAIRS ONLY, AND THE ARM IS STILL RUNNING. b0_moe48_8b was at step 1000 of 10,172 when this was measured (status `running` in runs/experiments.jsonl, log mtime 2026-09-06 03:32Z, 5 val points). The comparators end at step 3815, so they can pair no further than MoE step 1271 whatever the 8B arm reaches -- past that there is no matched-token comparator at all. The gap's late behaviour is therefore unmeasured, and the last two pairs (+0.037 then +0.038 for dense, +0.067 then +0.066 for MoE) sit inside a range too narrow to call a direction on two points.
facts.boundary: GLOBAL BATCH 192 vs 64, a 3x difference, and it is not separable from the token axis here: the 8B-token arm was launched at the larger batch, so 'more tokens' and 'larger batch' move together across every pair. THE COMPARATORS' WSD WARMDOWN CAPS THIS COMPARISON AT ARM STEP 1144, so the five pairs above are the whole usable range and no sixth pair extends it: train.warmdown_start returns total - max(1, int(cfg.warmdown * total)), which at warmdown 0.1 is comparator step 3434 of 3815 against arm step 9155 of 10172. Any pair past comparator step 3434 compares an annealing model to a stable-lr one. MEASURED on b0_e1p_dense 2026-09-06: lr is 1.00e-02 through step 3400 and 5.41e-04 by 3800, and val falls 2.259 (3400) to 2.194 (3600) to 2.128 (3800) on the decaying lr rather than on tokens; the arm's step 1200 pairs with comparator step 3600 and yields a gap that reads as the gap re-widening after 0.79B when what changed is that one side began annealing. The instrument marks such pairs ANNEALED-vs-STABLE and counts them rather than dropping them. WARMUP IS 300 STEPS ABSOLUTE in all three arms, which is 2.9% of the 8B arm's 10,172 steps and 7.9% of a comparator's 3,815 -- so at any matched-token point the 8B arm is further past its warmup, and the earliest pairs are where that matters most (step 200 of the 8B arm is 0.16B tokens but only 66% of the way through its own warmup). THE BALANCER IS ON in every MoE arm (moe_bias_gamma 0.001), and its load_gini on the 8B arm rises from 0.029 at step 300 to 0.596 at step 1000 while entropy_norm falls 0.9996 -> 0.7939 (runs/moe_diag.jsonl, name moe48_8b), so routing is still moving over exactly the window these pairs cover. ARCHITECTURE IS CONFOUNDED WITH BATCH AND WARMUP in this pair, and that is the whole difference from moe.equal_token_gap_vs_moe48_small_batch: this comparator is dense, so a reader cannot attribute any part of the gap to the MoE architecture from this fact alone. The MoE-vs-MoE fact holds architecture fixed and is the sharper of the two; this one answers 'what does the 8B MoE run reach against the dense recipe at matched tokens', with three things moving at once.

facts.value: At matched tokens the 8B-token MoE-48 arm is WORSE than the same architecture trained at one-third the global batch, by +0.7400 nat at 0.16B narrowing to +0.0660 at 0.79B. With architecture held fixed, the residual gap is what batch 192 vs 64 and the 2.9%-vs-7.9% warmup fraction cost at this token budget -- it does NOT say the larger batch is worse asymptotically, only that it is behind at every point where a comparator exists.

facts.value: At matched steps and matched global batch the 8B-token MoE-48 arm is BELOW the batch-matched dense arm at all nine in-training val points, by 0.030 to 0.096 nat. The sign is opposite to moe.equal_token_gap_vs_dense_0p2b, whose comparator ran at batch 64. NO DIRECTION IS CLAIMED: the series is not monotone -- it reverses at step(s) 7000, 10000 -- so the range above is the claim and a peak location is not, an extremum's position having moved once already between the 7-point and 8-point reads of this same series. Pairs: 2000: 2.216 vs 2.246 = -0.030; 3000: 2.103 vs 2.161 = -0.058; 4000: 2.044 vs 2.115 = -0.071; 5000: 2.013 vs 2.093 = -0.080; 6000: 1.971 vs 2.056 = -0.085; 7000: 1.946 vs 2.023 = -0.077; 8000: 1.921 vs 2.002 = -0.081; 9000: 1.896 vs 1.992 = -0.096; 10000: 1.795 vs 1.884 = -0.089.
facts.source: Both arms' own run logs ON THE POD, read through ~/bin/pod, not present in the repo: /work/aupai/runs/1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.log (MoE-48, 48 routed experts, top_k 3, expert_ffn 768, 1 shared, moe_layers 0-11, moe_bias_gamma 0.001) and /work/aupai/runs/0.2b_8b_b192.log (dense, no moe_* keys in its cfg line). Rows matched on the literal `^step N/M val X` form at every thousand from 2000 to 10000; this entry's writer refuses to emit a partial series. THE MoE ARM'S LOG IS THE SECOND SEGMENT of its run: the first is /work/aupai/runs/b0_moe48_8b.log, which ends at step 1000 with signal 15, and the resume is named in the second segment's WSD JOIN line. The pairs above all lie past step 1000, so they are entirely inside the second segment and the resume does not enter them.

config.pairing_rule: MATCHED STEPS, because both arms run the same global batch: batch 8 x accum 4 x 6 cards = 786,432 tokens/step on each side, ratio 1. This is what distinguishes this fact from moe.equal_token_gap_vs_dense_0p2b, whose comparator ran 262,144 tokens/step at ratio 3 with step N against 3N. That comparator ALSO cannot reach this token count at all: it totals 3815 steps and anneals past 3434, so a pair beyond it compares an annealing model to a stable-lr one. A batch-matched comparator is not a different pairing convention here, it is the only pairing that exists at 7.86B tokens.
config.both_arms: total 10172 steps, warmdown 0.1, anneal_frac 0.0, warmup 300, val_every 200, seed 42, mix data/mix_200m_8b.json, seq 4096
config.warmup_share: 300 of 10172 = 2.9% on both arms, so warmup fraction is not a difference between them (it IS one against the batch-64 comparator, which carries 300 of 3815 = 7.9%)
config.lr_state: Warmdown begins at step 9155 on BOTH arms, from train.py's wd_steps = max(1, int(cfg.warmdown * total)) and wd_start = total - wd_steps; PROVENANCE CORRECTED 2026-09-07 by b0: this entry first said the run logs print it. Only the MoE arm's log does, in its `WSD JOIN:` line, which exists because that arm resumed at step 1000; the dense arm never resumed and `grep -c 9155` on its log returns 0. The value 9155 stands and equality across arms was re-verified from the logged lr itself rather than from a printed string: step 9000 1.00e-02, 9200 9.96e-03, 9400 8.71e-03, 10000 1.16e-03, identical on both arms. Pairs 2000-9000 therefore sit at constant lr and the 10000 pair is 845 steps into annealing. MoE's val falls 1.896 -> 1.795 across that boundary, a drop driven by lr and not by tokens. The pair remains valid because the two arms share total and warmdown and so anneal identically from the same step, but it is NOT the same quantity as the eight constant-lr pairs and a trend must not be extended through it.

facts.uncertainty: Single seed (42) on each side, so no seed spread is available and none is claimed. val is the in-training figure at val_every 200, one number per point, not a re-scored evaluation. NEITHER ARM'S HOST WAS CONTROLLED: the MoE arm ran 12:xx-13:09Z with card 6's occupancy unrecorded, and the dense arm's window spans a 95 GB backup (14:31:57-15:24:10Z on /mnt/data02). That affects step TIME, measured separately, and no mechanism is claimed by which it would move val -- but it is recorded here because it was not held fixed.
facts.boundary: PER-DOMAIN ATTRIBUTION IS NOT IN THIS ENTRY. A single val number cannot say whether the gap is code, math, zh_web, or spread evenly, and that is what decides where the extra parameters are spent; it is entry 2, from the --profile control rows at step 10000. ALSO NOT SEPARABLE HERE: batch and architecture are held together with the token axis only in the sense that both arms match on batch -- what this entry does not isolate is the 1.28B extra parameters against the routing itself, since the arms differ in both at once. moe.equal_token_gap_vs_moe48_small_batch is the pair that isolates batch and warmup share with architecture fixed, and it should be read beside this one rather than combined with it.

facts.value: Per-domain split of the MoE-48-vs-batch-matched-dense gap, at TWO pairing points. dense-minus-MoE is POSITIVE in all nine domains at both points (MoE lower everywhere), and the split is chat-heavy at both: the two chat domains (chat_qa, chatml) are 2 of 9 domains and take 39.9% of the summed gap at 3.93B and 50.1% at 7.86B, while the two code domains take 10.7% and 9.8%. Nine-domain unweighted means: +0.0943 nat at 3.93B (step5000 pins, rows 82/83) and +0.1254 at 7.86B (endpoints, rows 80/81). THE MEAN'S GROWTH IS NOT A PER-DOMAIN DIRECTION: the summed gap rises +0.2797 between the points and 80.9% of that rise is the two chat domains, while 2 of 9 domains SHRINK (cot, en_c4_stage2). 3.93B: chat_qa +0.1718 (20.2%); chatml +0.1670 (19.7%); en_c4_stage2 +0.1112 (13.1%); math_owm_stage2 +0.0904 (10.7%); textbook_30b +0.0775 (9.1%); zh_web +0.0735 (8.7%); cot +0.0665 (7.8%); code_py_starcoder +0.0496 (5.8%); code_py_rp1t +0.0410 (4.8%). 7.86B: chat_qa +0.2873 (25.5%); chatml +0.2779 (24.6%); en_c4_stage2 +0.1092 (9.7%); zh_web +0.0996 (8.8%); math_owm_stage2 +0.0919 (8.1%); textbook_30b +0.0868 (7.7%); cot +0.0653 (5.8%); code_py_rp1t +0.0602 (5.3%); code_py_starcoder +0.0500 (4.4%).
facts.source: Four doc_cu rows in runs/score_matrix.jsonl IN THIS REPO, lines 80 (ckpt_1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.pt#cu), 81 (ckpt_0.2b_8b_b192.pt#cu), 82 (ckpt_1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.milestone_matchedtok_step5000.pt#cu), 83 (ckpt_0.2b_8b_b192.milestone_matchedtok_step5000.pt#cu). All four from the identical command, ckpt the only difference: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python3 eval/score_matrix.py --ckpt <C> --metrics domain_loss --cu_path doc_cu --ngpu 1 --mix data/mix_200m_8b.json --json runs/score_matrix.jsonl`. The rows were written on the pod's emptyDir and pulled with scripts/pod_pull_ledgers.py --apply, which is why they can be cited: an emptyDir row vanishes when the pod is deleted. This entry's writer refuses if any of the four is absent, if they disagree on vocab_id/profile/_split or the domain set, or if a row's stored unweighted_mean disagrees with the mean recomputed from its own nine losses (max observed disagreement 4.4e-05, a rounding artefact of the stored 4-decimal figure).

config.extends: moe.equal_token_gap_vs_dense_b192, which recorded one in-training val number per point and states in its own boundary that per-domain attribution is not in it. This is that attribution. It is a DIFFERENT STATISTIC on a different corpus: doc_cu nine-domain scoring at profile full, not the in-training val figure. The two disagree in size and the difference is not explained here -- at step5000 doc_cu +0.0943 against val +0.0800, at step10000 doc_cu +0.1254 against val +0.0890.
